question: How does SQLAlchemy's Session work and what is the unit of work pattern?
title: SQLAlchemy Session and Unit of Work
direct_answer: Session is a unit of work: add objects with session.add(), update by mutating tracked objects, delete with session.delete(). session.flush() sends SQL to DB without committing. session.commit() commits the transaction. session.rollback() undoes since last commit. In FastAPI: yield a session per request, commit on success, rollback on exception. The Session tracks all loaded objects and detects changes via the identity map.
interviewer_intent: Tests understanding of SQLAlchemy's core abstraction — the session is not just a connection, it's a stateful unit of work.

sections.title: Session as unit of work
sections.content:
SQLAlchemy Session maintains an identity map: once you load an object, subsequent queries return the same Python object. Mutations are tracked automatically — change user.email, and SQLAlchemy generates UPDATE on commit without an explicit save call.

Transaction boundary: a Session has exactly one active transaction. commit() flushes all pending changes to the DB and commits. Any exception after flush should trigger rollback() — otherwise partial changes may be visible.

Flush vs commit: flush sends SQL to the DB within the current transaction but doesn't commit. Useful for getting a server-generated ID (autoincrement) before committing. commit finalizes.

sections.title: Session patterns
sections.content:
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession, create_async_engine, async_sessionmaker

engine = create_async_engine('postgresql+asyncpg://user:pw@localhost/db')
async_session = async_sessionmaker(engine, expire_on_commit=False)

# FastAPI dependency
async def get_db():
    async with async_session() as session:
        try:
            yield session
            await session.commit()
        except Exception:
            await session.rollback()
            raise

# CRUD operations
async def create_user(db: AsyncSession, email: str) -> User:
    user = User(email=email)
    db.add(user)
    await db.flush()   # get id without committing
    return user        # user.id is now set

async def update_user(db: AsyncSession, user: User, new_email: str) -> User:
    user.email = new_email   # just mutate — Session tracks it
    return user  # committed by dependency

async def delete_user(db: AsyncSession, user: User) -> None:
    await db.delete(user)

seo.metaDescription: SQLAlchemy Session unit of work: identity map, flush vs commit, rollback patterns, and async session in FastAPI dependency injection.

speakable_v2.hook: SQLAlchemy Session is not just a connection wrapper — it's a stateful unit of work that tracks every object you've loaded.

beats.content: The Session maintains an identity map. Load the same user twice, get the same Python object. Mutate it once and SQLAlchemy generates the UPDATE — no explicit save call needed.
flush sends SQL within the transaction — useful to get a server-generated ID. commit finalizes and clears the transaction. rollback undoes everything since the last commit.

speakable_v2.cap: expire_on_commit=False in async code: without it, accessing attributes after commit triggers a new query — in async code that can fail because the session context may be closed.
